title: Reading documents
passage:
Volunteer brief | Kōwhai Hall supper
This is our first shared supper since the hall reopened. The supper will be in the main hall. We have plates, mugs and serving utensils. The kitchen is not ready for use, so anything offered to the supper table must be ready to serve when it arrives.

The craft table by the foyer is collecting handmade items for a prize draw. Items left there will be given to winners. At the supper table, guests can serve food from their own dishes and take the empty dishes home, or ask us to transfer the food to a hall platter.

The electrical crew replaced the lights above the serving tables, not the ones along the wall. The portable screen can stand either along the wall or between the two serving tables. From its place between the tables it cuts off the light from the ceiling fitting above the far table before that light reaches the name cards on the near table. The wall lights do not shine onto the cards from either position.

The hall has windows on the street side and on the yard side. Either set can be opened for fresh air. Please leave a clear path to the ones volunteers will use; we won’t be able to move furniture easily once people are sitting down.

Several supper guests saw Lani come back carrying the missing hall key. She handed it back to the desk, out of their sight. One guest has already asked her whether she can let the craft group in early next week. Our craft signup cards name the person leading each class, for questions about the activity. The staffed desk keeps the key and can arrange entry outside the class hours.

Moana’s note to Tom before the supper
Hi, Tom. Before you send the invitation, could you reword ‘bring a plate’? The regulars know what it means, but yesterday someone asked if an empty saucer would do. I told him to bring enough for a few people to try. Let’s not promise anyone the use of an oven.

Sera showed me the platter she helped paint at the craft class. It looks like one of the prizes, so she asked me to make clear that only the slices on it are for sharing. The platter is her neighbor’s. She asked if we could take it off her hands when she arrives, then added that she promised to bring it straight back to her neighbor once she’d dropped off the slices. She’ll be gone before people start eating.

For your thank-you at the start, I heard back from the library: the loose cushions were theirs. They’re pleased we can use them for supper, but want them back afterward. I asked Lani if you could mention her when you thank the people who got the hall ready. She laughed. “I’ll take mine when we’re stacking the chairs. And I’d put a line in the welcome for the people coming back next week. Finding a key doesn’t make you the one on duty.”

One small thing about setting up the room: yesterday I tried opening the street windows and had to repeat myself every time a bus went past. When I shut those and opened the yard windows, we could hear one another again and the room felt just as fresh.

One more thing for the next supper: in the test run we could read the name cards at both tables with just the ceiling lights on. Then we put the screen between the tables to hide the spare chairs from the queue. Nobody touched the switches, but I could no longer read the cards at the near table. I’d rather not ask the electrical crew back unless we really need them. Thanks, Moana
passageZh:
志工簡報｜科懷會堂聚餐
這是會堂重新開放後第一次共餐，地點在主廳。會堂已備有餐盤、馬克杯和分菜用具。廚房還不能用，送到共餐桌的食物必須一送到就能上桌。

門廳旁的手作桌正在募集抽獎用的手作品。放到手作桌的物品會送給得獎者。來賓可用自家的盤子盛放食物，吃完再把空盤帶回家，也可以請我們把食物移到會堂的大盤上。

電工班更換的是餐檯上方的燈，不是沿牆的燈。活動屏風可以靠牆放，也可以放在兩張餐檯之間。擺在兩張餐檯之間時，屏風會擋住遠端餐檯上方的燈光，使光照不到近端餐檯上的菜名卡。不論屏風擺在哪裡，沿牆的燈光都照不到菜名卡。

主廳有兩側的窗戶，一側面向街道，另一側面向院子，打開任一側都能通風。請留出通往志工會用的窗戶的走道；大家坐下後，就不容易再挪動家具。

有幾位聚餐來賓看見拉妮帶著遺失的會堂鑰匙回來。她在來賓看不見的地方把鑰匙交回櫃檯。已有人問她，下週能不能提早讓手作小組進場。手作課的報名卡會寫上各班帶領人的姓名，方便大家詢問活動內容。鑰匙由服務櫃檯保管，課程時段之外的進場也由櫃檯安排。

聚餐前莫阿娜寄給湯姆的信
湯姆，你好。寄出邀請前，可以換個方式寫「帶一盤來」嗎？常來的人知道那是什麼意思，但昨天有人問帶一只空茶碟行不行。我跟他說，帶夠幾個人嚐嚐的份量就好。我們不要答應讓人用烤箱。

賽拉給我看她在手作課幫忙彩繪的大盤。看起來很像其中一件抽獎品，所以她請我說清楚：只有盤上的切片點心要和大家分享。大盤是她鄰居的。她先問她一到時，我們能不能接手這只盤子，又補充說，她答應放下點心後就要直接把盤子還給鄰居。大家開動前她就會離開。

關於開場致謝，我收到圖書館回覆：那些散放的坐墊是他們的。他們很樂意借我們聚餐用，但用完要歸還。我問拉妮，你謝謝布置會堂的人時，能不能提到她。她笑著說：「等我們疊椅子時，再謝我就好。開場最好也給下週還會來的人一句提醒。找到鑰匙可不代表那個人就負責值班。」

另外還有一點關於場地布置：昨天我試著開街道那側的窗，每次有公車經過，我都得把話再說一遍。我把那側的窗關上，改開院子那側，大家又聽得清彼此說話，室內也一樣通風。

下次聚餐還有一件事要留意：試擺時，只開天花板的燈，兩張餐檯上的菜名卡都看得清楚。後來我們把屏風挪到兩張餐檯之間，擋住排隊的人看向備用椅的視線。沒有人動過開關，但我再也看不清近端餐檯上的菜名卡了。我想，除非真的有需要，不然先不要請電工班再跑一趟。 謝謝，莫阿娜
